prompt:
Implement `Eval(doc any, path string) ([]any, error)` in the Go package in the repository root (`jsonpath.go`; it is currently a stub that always fails). It evaluates a tiny JSONPath subset over a document decoded by encoding/json into an `any`: `$`, `.name`, `['name']`, `[n]`, `[*]` and `..name`.

README.md specifies everything precisely: the exact syntax (and which paths are syntax errors), what each segment selects, the exact order of the results (including how object members are ordered and the order in which `..name` visits a document), what a path that selects nothing returns, and when an error is returned. This subset deliberately differs from full JSONPath in places (for example there is no `.*`, no negative index, and `..` only takes a plain name), so follow the README, not your memory of JSONPath. More tests than the visible ones, covering the rest of the README, are run when your work is checked.

`jsonpath_test.go` holds the README examples; do not edit any *_test.go file. Check your work with `go test ./...`.
